displayName: loop-sessions: analytics export more than 3 h behind

conditions.displayName: export lag_seconds (p50 over 1 h) above 3 h
no export run line for 3 h (the job is not running)

documentation.content:
The BigQuery copy of the derived tables (dataset loop_sessions, bucket __ANALYTICS_BUCKET__) is more than three hours behind Postgres, or the hourly export job has not written its run line for three hours. The reader is unaffected; analysts querying BigQuery are reading stale data.

Expected while a catch-up is in progress: the first run after provisioning, and the runs after a long outage, take at most 2,000 sessions (or 40 session start days) and 6 event days each (server/export, Options) and report the lag honestly until the corpus is exported, about seven hourly runs for the whole corpus. Check whether the lag is falling: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloud_run_job" AND resource.labels.job_name="loop-sessions-export" AND jsonPayload.message="export run"' --limit=6 --freshness=6h --format='value(timestamp,jsonPayload.status,jsonPayload.lag_seconds,jsonPayload.partitions,jsonPayload.capped,jsonPayload.error)'`. Falling with `capped=true` is a catch-up; nothing to do.

Not falling: the status of the last runs says why. `failed` with `failed_loads` above zero is a BigQuery load the `export load failed` line names (table, day, job id, the API's message; a schema mismatch means tables.sql lacks a column the projection gained, fix the DDL and re-run provision.sh). `timeout` is a run that did not finish inside its budget: look at the partition lines for the slow table. No run line at all: the Cloud Scheduler job loop-sessions-export-hourly or the Cloud Run job is disabled or failing to start (`gcloud run jobs executions list --job=loop-sessions-export --region=<region> --limit=5`).

Runbook: examples/deploy-gcp/README.md#runbook-export
